PTx unveils ArrowTube and expands into autonomous tillage

Farm Progress Show: ArrowTube uses engineered friction and centrifugal force to position corn seeds tip forward for optimal growth.

Chris Torres,Editor,American AgriculturistSeptember 3, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

ArrowTube is designed to orient corn seeds in the ground to optimize emergence and yield. Photos by Chris Torres 

Subscribe to Farm Progress AGTech — our free, twice-weekly newsletter delivering the latest innovations, emerging technologies and expert insights to your inbox.

PTx, Agco’s precision ag division, is releasing a next-gen seed delivery system by the end of the year as well as updating its autonomous retrofit kit for tillage.

ArrowTube, sold under Precision Planting, is designed to orient corn seeds in the ground to optimize emergence and yield.

Here’s how it works: Seeds from a V-set meter are accelerated through an engineered loop with “strategic friction” — specific bumps and ridges that orient seeds tip forward. The seeds then travel through a rifle-like corkscrew path where centrifugal force maintains spacing and orientation. At the bottom, a knife cuts a narrow sub-furrow below the disk openers, and seeds slot into the furrow at high speed.

Bryce Baker, North American marketing lead for PTx, said the system helps address a key agronomic challenge: When seeds aren’t properly oriented, roots and shoots must bend to find the correct direction for growth.

Related:Favorite products from FPS26

“If you point it tip down, the radical root can come straight out the tip and grow down. The coleoptile comes out, and the embryo grows up. If we have some other orientation, the coleoptile or radical root might have to make a 90-degree turn, a 180-degree turn. It’s burning energy and time to emergence when it has to do that,” he said.

The company is targeting a late-year limited commercial launch with full launch by next July. But compatibility is limited to John Deere row units — XP and MaxEmerge 5 and above — and Precision Planting Cornerstone row units.

Autonomous kit now does tillage

OutRun, an autonomous grain cart system by PTx Trimble that was introduced two years ago for grain carts, has been expanded into tillage functions.

The hardware kit includes a rooftop unit with Starlink and GPS receivers, plus lidar and radar mounted on the front of the tractor. Operators can monitor speed, engine rpm, fuel levels and equipment performance via a phone app.

The system can do spring and fall tillage, and land rolling, with a camera array providing live feed monitoring.

Current compatibility is limited to John Deere 8R tractors and select Fendt models, with John Deere 9R compatibility coming later this year.

The cost is around $65,000 for a full tillage or grain cart setup (with one combine), plus $15,000 annually for Starlink subscription, GNSS corrections and system updates.

Symphony Vision expands availability

The company’s answer to computer vision and AI-powered spot spraying, Symphony Vision, is slated for full commercial availability in time for next year’s growing season.

Related:2027 Farm Progress Show returns to Decatur, Ill.

Symphony Vision can be retrofitted to sprayers from John Deere, Case IH, Hagie, Apache and more.

Just like Greeneye and John Deere See & Spray, it uses cameras mounted on the boom that can distinguish between weeds and crops. But there are no subscription fees or per-acre charges.

It comes in three versions: Spot, Rate and Duo. The most advanced, Duo, has a two-nozzle system: one nozzle that broadcasts residual herbicides and fertilizers across an entire field, and another that applies contact herbicides only where weeds are detected.

“So, you don’t have to sacrifice, and you can do that all in one pass,” Baker said.

Prices start at $35,000 for basic nozzle control to around $150,000 for the full Duo system.

“If you think about whatever percentage of herbicide savings you have, there’s some fast savings that happen with that pretty quick,” he said.

For more information go to ptxag.com.

About the Author

Chris Torres

Editor, American Agriculturist

Chris Torres, editor of American Agriculturist, previously worked at Lancaster Farming, where he started in 2006 as a staff writer and later became regional editor. Torres is a seven-time winner of the Keystone Press Awards, handed out by the Pennsylvania Press Association, and he is a Pennsylvania State University graduate.

Torres says he wants American Agriculturist to be farmers' "go-to product, continuing the legacy and high standard (former American Agriculturist editor) John Vogel has set." Torres succeeds Vogel, who retired after 47 years with Farm Progress and its related publications.

"The news business is a challenging job," Torres says. "It makes you think outside your small box, and you have to formulate what the reader wants to see from the overall product. It's rewarding to see a nice product in the end."

Torres' family is based in Lebanon County, Pa. His wife grew up on a small farm in Berks County, Pa., where they raised corn, soybeans, feeder cattle and more. Torres and his wife are parents to three young boys.

translationZh:
PTx是爱科（Agco）旗下的精准农业部门，计划在年底前发布下一代种子递送系统，同时更新其用于耕整地作业的自动驾驶改装套件。

ArrowTube以Precision Planting品牌销售，旨在让玉米种子在土壤中以正确的姿态定位，从而优化出苗和产量。

其工作原理如下：来自V-set计量器的种子被加速通过一个带有“策略性摩擦”的工程管道——管道内特定的凸起和棱线使种子尖端朝前定向。随后种子通过类似来复枪膛线的螺旋路径，利用离心力保持间距和方向。在管道底部，一把切刀在开沟盘下方切出一条狭窄的亚种沟，种子以高速落入沟中。

PTx北美市场负责人布莱斯·贝克（Bryce Baker）表示，该系统有助于解决一个关键的农艺难题：当种子朝向不正确时，根和芽必须弯曲才能找到正确的生长方向。

“如果种子尖端朝下，胚根可以直接从尖端伸出向下生长。胚芽鞘伸出后，胚向上生长。如果是其他朝向，胚芽鞘或胚根可能不得不转90度甚至180度的弯。这样一来，出苗就会消耗额外的能量和时间。”他说。

公司计划在年底前进行限量商业发布，明年7月全面上市。但兼容性仅限于约翰迪尔（John Deere）行单元——XP和MaxEmerge 5及以上型号——以及Precision Planting Cornerstone行单元。

**自动驾驶套件现已支持耕整地作业**

OutRun是PTx Trimble两年前针对谷物运输车推出的自动驾驶系统，现已扩展至耕整地功能。

该硬件套件包括一个带有Starlink和GPS接收器的屋顶单元，以及安装在拖拉机前部的激光雷达和毫米波雷达。操作员可通过手机应用监控速度、发动机转速、燃油油位和设备性能。

该系统可进行春季和秋季耕整地作业以及土地镇压，摄像头阵列提供实时画面监控。

目前的兼容性仅限于约翰迪尔8R系列拖拉机和部分芬特（Fendt）型号，约翰迪尔9R系列的兼容性将于今年晚些时候推出。

整套耕整地或谷物运输配置（含一台联合收割机）的成本约为65,000美元，另加每年15,000美元的Starlink订阅费、GNSS校正和系统更新费用。

**Symphony Vision扩大供应范围**

该公司针对计算机视觉和AI精准喷施的解决方案Symphony Vision，计划在明年种植季前全面商用。

Symphony Vision可加装到约翰迪尔、凯斯IH（Case IH）、Hagie、Apache等品牌的喷雾机上。

与Greeneye和约翰迪尔See & Spray一样，它使用安装在喷杆上的摄像头来区分杂草和作物。但不同之处在于，它没有订阅费或按亩收费。

该产品有三个版本：Spot、Rate和Duo。最先进的Duo版本采用双喷嘴系统：一个喷嘴在整个田间播撒残留性除草剂和肥料，另一个喷嘴仅在检测到杂草的地方施用触杀型除草剂。

“这样你就不必做出取舍，而且可以一次完成所有作业，”贝克说。

价格从基础喷嘴控制版的35,000美元到全套Duo系统的约150,000美元不等。

“想想你能节省多少百分比的除草剂用量，很快就能收回成本，”他说。

更多信息请访问ptxag.com。
